entries.subject: Arithmetic
entries.name: nth Odd Number
entries.searchText: nth odd number nth odd number = 2n − 1 a_n = 2n - 1 odd numbers form the sequence 1, 3, 5, 7, … the nth odd number is obtained by doubling n and subtracting 1. find the 8th odd number. a_8 = 2×8 − 1 = 16 − 1 = 15. so the 8th odd number is 15. class 6 pattern rule only — not an algebraic identity of higher classes. arithmetic patterns in mathematics class 6 cbse odd pattern sequence 2n-1 cbse class 6 patterns

entries.subject: Arithmetic
entries.name: nth Even Number
entries.searchText: nth even number nth even number = 2n a_n = 2n even numbers form the sequence 2, 4, 6, 8, … the nth even number is twice n. find the 9th even number. a_9 = 2×9 = 18. for n = 1, the first even counting number in this pattern is taken as 2. arithmetic patterns in mathematics class 6 cbse even pattern sequence 2n cbse class 6 patterns

entries.subject: Arithmetic
entries.name: nth Triangular Number
entries.searchText: nth triangular number t_n = n(n + 1)/2 t_n = \frac{n(n+1)}{2} triangular numbers count dots arranged in a triangular pattern: 1, 3, 6, 10, 15, … find t_5. t_5 = 5×6/2 = 15. this is a class 6 pattern formula, not a mensuration area formula. arithmetic patterns in mathematics class 6 cbse triangular pattern t_n cbse class 6 patterns

entries.subject: Arithmetic
entries.name: nth Square Number
entries.searchText: nth square number s_n = n² s_n = n^2 square numbers are 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, … obtained by multiplying a number by itself. find the 6th square number. s_6 = 6² = 36. arithmetic patterns in mathematics class 6 cbse square number pattern cbse class 6 patterns

entries.subject: Arithmetic
entries.name: nth Cube Number
entries.searchText: nth cube number c_n = n³ c_n = n^3 cube numbers are 1, 8, 27, 64, … obtained by multiplying a number by itself three times. find the 4th cube number. c_4 = 4³ = 64. cube numbers as patterns only; solid volume formulas belong to higher classes. arithmetic patterns in mathematics class 6 cbse cube number pattern cbse class 6 patterns

entries.subject: Arithmetic
entries.name: Fibonacci Sequence Rule
entries.searchText: fibonacci sequence rule f_n = f_{n−1} + f_{n−2} (with f_1 = 1, f_2 = 1) f_n = f_{n-1} + f_{n-2},\quad f_1=1,\ f_2=1 each fibonacci number is the sum of the two numbers before it: 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, … find f_7. sequence: 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13. so f_7 = 13. starting values may be shown as 1, 1 or 0, 1 depending on convention. arithmetic patterns in mathematics class 6 cbse fibonacci pattern sequence cbse class 6 patterns

entries.subject: Arithmetic
entries.name: Place Value of a Digit
entries.formula: Place value = digit × value of its place
entries.searchText: place value of a digit place value = digit × value of its place \text{place value} = d \times 10^{k} the place value of a digit depends on its position in the number (ones, tens, hundreds, …). in 4,582 the place value of 5 is 5 × 100 = 500. face value of a digit is the digit itself; place value depends on position. arithmetic number play class 6 cbse place value digit number cbse class 6 number play

entries.subject: Arithmetic
entries.name: Expanded Form of a Number
entries.formula: Number = sum of (each digit × its place value)
entries.searchText: expanded form of a number number = sum of (each digit × its place value) n = \sum d_i \times 10^{i} expanded form writes a number as the sum of the place values of its digits. 3,406 = 3×1000 + 4×100 + 0×10 + 6×1 = 3000 + 400 + 6. arithmetic number play class 6 cbse expanded form place value cbse class 6 number play

entries.subject: Arithmetic
entries.name: Factor Relation
entries.formula: If a is a factor of b, then b = a × k for some whole number k
entries.searchText: factor relation if a is a factor of b, then b = a × k for some whole number k b = a \times k a factor of a number divides it exactly, leaving no remainder. 4 is a factor of 20 because 20 = 4 × 5. 1 is a factor of every whole number; every number is a factor of itself. arithmetic prime time class 6 cbse factor divides cbse class 6 factors

entries.subject: Arithmetic
entries.name: Multiple Relation
entries.searchText: multiple relation multiples of a = a, 2a, 3a, 4a, … m = a \times n \ (n = 1,2,3,\ldots) multiples of a number are obtained by multiplying it by 1, 2, 3, … multiples of 5 include 5, 10, 15, 20, … arithmetic prime time class 6 cbse multiple times table common multiple cbse class 6 multiples

entries.subject: Arithmetic
entries.name: Divisibility Rule for 2
entries.formula: A number is divisible by 2 if its ones digit is 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8
entries.searchText: divisibility rule for 2 a number is divisible by 2 if its ones digit is 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8 \text{ones digit} \in \{0,2,4,6,8\} even numbers are exactly the numbers divisible by 2. 148 ends with 8, so 148 is divisible by 2. arithmetic prime time class 6 cbse divisibility divisible by 2 cbse class 6 divisibility

entries.subject: Arithmetic
entries.name: Divisibility Rule for 3
entries.formula: A number is divisible by 3 if the sum of its digits is divisible by 3
entries.searchText: divisibility rule for 3 a number is divisible by 3 if the sum of its digits is divisible by 3 \sum \text{digits} \equiv 0 \pmod{3} check divisibility by 3 without long division. for 252: 2+5+2=9, and 9 is divisible by 3, so 252 is divisible by 3. you may repeatedly sum digits until a single digit remains. arithmetic prime time class 6 cbse divisibility by 3 cbse class 6 divisibility

entries.subject: Arithmetic
entries.name: Divisibility Rule for 5
entries.formula: A number is divisible by 5 if its ones digit is 0 or 5
entries.searchText: divisibility rule for 5 a number is divisible by 5 if its ones digit is 0 or 5 \text{ones digit} \in \{0,5\} numbers ending in 0 or 5 are divisible by 5. 680 ends with 0, so it is divisible by 5. arithmetic prime time class 6 cbse divisibility by 5 cbse class 6 divisibility

entries.subject: Arithmetic
entries.name: Divisibility Rule for 9
entries.formula: A number is divisible by 9 if the sum of its digits is divisible by 9
entries.searchText: divisibility rule for 9 a number is divisible by 9 if the sum of its digits is divisible by 9 \sum \text{digits} \equiv 0 \pmod{9} similar to the rule for 3, but the digit sum must be divisible by 9. for 729: 7+2+9=18, and 18 is divisible by 9, so 729 is divisible by 9. arithmetic prime time class 6 cbse divisibility by 9 cbse class 6 divisibility

entries.subject: Arithmetic
entries.name: Divisibility Rule for 10
entries.formula: A number is divisible by 10 if its ones digit is 0
entries.searchText: divisibility rule for 10 a number is divisible by 10 if its ones digit is 0 \text{ones digit} = 0 a number ending with 0 is divisible by 10. 940 ends with 0, so it is divisible by 10. arithmetic prime time class 6 cbse divisibility by 10 cbse class 6 divisibility

entries.subject: Arithmetic
entries.name: HCF × LCM Relation (Two Numbers)
entries.formula: HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b) = a × b
entries.searchText: hcf × lcm relation (two numbers) hcf(a, b) × lcm(a, b) = a × b \mathrm{hcf}(a,b)\times \mathrm{lcm}(a,b)=a\times b for any two positive integers, the product of their hcf and lcm equals the product of the numbers. for 12 and 18: hcf=6, lcm=36. check: 6×36=216 and 12×18=216. this relation is stated for two numbers. arithmetic prime time class 6 cbse hcf lcm cbse class 6 hcf lcm

entries.subject: Arithmetic
entries.name: Fraction Notation
entries.searchText: fraction notation fraction = a/b (b ≠ 0) \frac{a}{b},\quad b \neq 0 a fraction represents equal parts of a whole. 3 equal slices out of 8 give the fraction 3/8. denominator cannot be zero. arithmetic fractions class 6 cbse fraction numerator denominator cbse class 6 fractions

entries.subject: Arithmetic
entries.name: Equivalent Fractions
entries.formula: a/b = (a × k)/(b × k) for any natural number k
entries.searchText: equivalent fractions a/b = (a × k)/(b × k) for any natural number k \frac{a}{b} = \frac{a \times k}{b \times k} multiplying numerator and denominator by the same non-zero number gives an equivalent fraction. 2/3 = (2×4)/(3×4) = 8/12. arithmetic fractions class 6 cbse equivalent fractions cbse class 6 fractions

entries.subject: Arithmetic
entries.name: Addition of Like Fractions
entries.searchText: addition of like fractions a/c + b/c = (a + b)/c \frac{a}{c}+\frac{b}{c}=\frac{a+b}{c} when denominators are the same, add the numerators and keep the denominator. 2/7 + 3/7 = 5/7. for unlike fractions, first make denominators equal. arithmetic fractions class 6 cbse add fractions like fractions cbse class 6 fractions

entries.subject: Arithmetic
entries.name: Subtraction of Like Fractions
entries.searchText: subtraction of like fractions a/c − b/c = (a − b)/c \frac{a}{c}-\frac{b}{c}=\frac{a-b}{c} when denominators are the same, subtract the numerators and keep the denominator. 7/10 − 3/10 = 4/10 = 2/5. arithmetic fractions class 6 cbse subtract fractions cbse class 6 fractions

entries.subject: Arithmetic
entries.name: Improper Fraction to Mixed Number
entries.formula: a/b = q + r/b, where a = q×b + r
entries.searchText: improper fraction to mixed number a/b = q + r/b, where a = q×b + r \frac{a}{b} = q + \frac{r}{b},\quad a = qb + r divide numerator by denominator; quotient is the whole part and remainder forms the fractional part. 17/5 = 3 + 2/5, because 17 = 3×5 + 2 (mixed number: 3 2/5). arithmetic fractions class 6 cbse improper fraction mixed number cbse class 6 fractions

entries.subject: Arithmetic
entries.name: Absolute Value
entries.formula: |a| = distance of a from 0 on the number line
entries.searchText: absolute value |a| = distance of a from 0 on the number line |a| = a \text{ if } a \ge 0;\quad |a| = -a \text{ if } a < 0 absolute value measures how far a number is from zero, ignoring direction. |−7| = 7 and |7| = 7. absolute value is never negative. arithmetic the other side of zero class 6 cbse absolute value integers cbse class 6 integers

entries.subject: Arithmetic
entries.name: Additive Inverse
entries.searchText: additive inverse a + (−a) = 0 a+(-a)=0 every integer has an opposite that sums with it to zero. the additive inverse of 9 is −9 because 9+(−9)=0. the additive inverse of 0 is 0. arithmetic the other side of zero class 6 cbse additive inverse integers cbse class 6 integers

entries.subject: Arithmetic
entries.name: Integer Addition on the Number Line
entries.formula: Add +k → move k units right; add −k → move k units left
entries.searchText: integer addition on the number line add +k → move k units right; add −k → move k units left a+(+k)\rightarrow\text{right};\ a+(-k)\rightarrow\text{left} integer addition can be modelled by moves on the number line. start at 3; add −5 → move 5 left → −2. so 3+(−5)=−2. class 6 emphasises number-line understanding of integer operations. arithmetic the other side of zero class 6 cbse integer addition number line cbse class 6 integers

entries.subject: Geometry
entries.name: Right Angle
entries.searchText: right angle right angle = 90° \angle=90^\circ an angle that measures exactly 90° is a right angle. the corner of a square page is a right angle (90°). acute < 90°, obtuse between 90° and 180°. geometry lines and angles class 6 cbse right angle 90 degrees cbse class 6 angles

entries.subject: Geometry
entries.name: Straight Angle
entries.searchText: straight angle straight angle = 180° \angle=180^\circ an angle that forms a straight line measures 180°. a straight angle looks like a straight line and measures 180°. geometry lines and angles class 6 cbse straight angle 180 degrees cbse class 6 angles

entries.subject: Geometry
entries.name: Complete Angle
entries.searchText: complete angle complete angle = 360° \angle=360^\circ a complete angle is one full rotation about a point. turning fully around to the same direction is a 360° turn. geometry lines and angles class 6 cbse complete angle 360 degrees cbse class 6 angles

entries.subject: Geometry
entries.name: Complementary Angles
entries.searchText: complementary angles ∠a + ∠b = 90° \angle a+\angle b=90^\circ two angles are complementary if their measures sum to 90°. if ∠a = 35°, complement = 90° − 35° = 55°. complementary angles need not be adjacent. geometry lines and angles class 6 cbse complementary angles cbse class 6 angles

entries.subject: Geometry
entries.name: Supplementary Angles
entries.searchText: supplementary angles ∠a + ∠b = 180° \angle a+\angle b=180^\circ two angles are supplementary if their measures sum to 180°. if ∠a = 110°, supplement = 180° − 110° = 70°. angles on a straight line are supplementary. geometry lines and angles class 6 cbse supplementary angles cbse class 6 angles

entries.subject: Geometry
entries.name: Circle Defined by Radius
entries.formula: A circle is the set of all points at fixed distance r from centre O
entries.searchText: circle defined by radius a circle is the set of all points at fixed distance r from centre o \{p: op=r\} with compass and ruler, a circle is drawn by keeping a constant radius from the centre. if radius is 4 cm, every point on the circle is 4 cm from the centre. class 6 focuses on construction; π-based circumference depth belongs later. geometry playing with constructions class 6 cbse circle radius construction cbse class 6 constructions

entries.subject: Geometry
entries.name: Perpendicular Bisector Property
entries.formula: Any point on the perpendicular bisector of AB is equidistant from A and B
entries.searchText: perpendicular bisector property any point on the perpendicular bisector of ab is equidistant from a and b pa=pb\text{ for }p\text{ on the perpendicular bisector of }ab the perpendicular bisector meets a segment at its midpoint at 90° and is the locus of equidistant points. if m is midpoint of ab and line l ⊥ ab at m, then for any p on l, pa = pb. geometry playing with constructions class 6 cbse perpendicular bisector construction cbse class 6 constructions

entries.subject: Geometry
entries.name: Line of Symmetry
entries.formula: A line of symmetry divides a figure into two mirror-image halves
entries.searchText: line of symmetry a line of symmetry divides a figure into two mirror-image halves \text{reflection across }\ell\text{ maps the figure onto itself} if one half of a figure is the mirror image of the other across a line, that line is a line of symmetry. a square has 4 lines of symmetry; a non-equilateral isosceles triangle has 1. some figures have no line of symmetry. geometry symmetry class 6 cbse line symmetry mirror cbse class 6 symmetry

entries.subject: Geometry
entries.name: Order of Rotational Symmetry
entries.formula: Order = 360° ÷ (smallest angle of rotation that maps the figure onto itself)
entries.searchText: order of rotational symmetry order = 360° ÷ (smallest angle of rotation that maps the figure onto itself) \text{order}=\frac{360^\circ}{\theta} rotational symmetry exists when a figure looks the same after a turn less than 360° about its centre. a square matches every 90°, so order = 360/90 = 4. every figure has order at least 1. geometry symmetry class 6 cbse rotational symmetry order cbse class 6 symmetry

entries.subject: Mensuration
entries.name: Perimeter of a Rectangle
entries.searchText: perimeter of a rectangle p = 2(l + b) p=2(l+b) perimeter is the total boundary length. a rectangle has two lengths and two breadths. if l=12 cm and b=5 cm, p=2(12+5)=34 cm. perimeter units are units of length. mensuration perimeter and area class 6 cbse perimeter rectangle cbse class 6 perimeter

entries.subject: Mensuration
entries.name: Perimeter of a Square
entries.searchText: perimeter of a square p = 4a p=4a all four sides of a square are equal, so perimeter is four times one side. if a=6 cm, p=4×6=24 cm. mensuration perimeter and area class 6 cbse perimeter square cbse class 6 perimeter

entries.subject: Mensuration
entries.name: Perimeter of a Triangle
entries.searchText: perimeter of a triangle p = a + b + c p=a+b+c the perimeter of a triangle is the sum of its three sides. sides 3 cm, 4 cm, 5 cm ⇒ p=12 cm. mensuration perimeter and area class 6 cbse perimeter triangle cbse class 6 perimeter

entries.subject: Mensuration
entries.name: Area of a Rectangle
entries.searchText: area of a rectangle a = l × b a=l\times b area measures the enclosed region. for a rectangle, area is length times breadth. if l=10 cm and b=4 cm, a=40 cm². area units are square units. perimeter and area are independent measures. mensuration perimeter and area class 6 cbse area rectangle cbse class 6 area

entries.subject: Mensuration
entries.name: Area of a Square
entries.searchText: area of a square a = a² a=a^2 area of a square is the side multiplied by itself. if a=9 cm, a=81 cm². a larger perimeter does not always mean a larger area. mensuration perimeter and area class 6 cbse area square cbse class 6 area

entries.subject: Data Handling
entries.name: Frequency
entries.formula: Frequency of an item = number of times it occurs in the data
entries.searchText: frequency frequency of an item = number of times it occurs in the data f(x)=\text{count of }x tally marks help count how often each value appears; that count is the frequency. in {2,3,2,2,5}, frequency of 2 is 3. tally marks are usually grouped in fives. data handling data handling and presentation class 6 cbse frequency tally data cbse class 6 data handling

entries.subject: Data Handling
entries.name: Pictograph Scale
entries.formula: Actual value = (number of symbols) × (value of one symbol)
entries.searchText: pictograph scale actual value = (number of symbols) × (value of one symbol) v=n\times s in a pictograph, each picture stands for a fixed number of items according to the scale. if 1 symbol = 10 students and 4 symbols are shown, value = 40. always read the key/scale before interpreting. data handling data handling and presentation class 6 cbse pictograph scale cbse class 6 data handling

entries.subject: Data Handling
entries.name: Bar Graph Reading
entries.formula: Value = (bar height in axis units) × (scale of the axis)
entries.searchText: bar graph reading value = (bar height in axis units) × (scale of the axis) v=h\times s a bar graph uses bars of equal width; bar length represents the value for each category. if scale is 1 unit = 5 and bar reaches 6 units, value = 30. bars should be equally spaced with clear labels. data handling data handling and presentation class 6 cbse bar graph scale cbse class 6 data handling
